lines: Kyle Grieve and Shawn O'Malley revisit Reddit after a roughly 25% one-day drop erased most of its gains, framing the key risk as Google's AI answers cannibalizing the organic search traffic that feeds Reddit's daily users.

They stress the financial strength despite the sell-off: gross margins above 90%, over $1 billion in annual free cash flow and minimal capex, though stock-based compensation must be offset by buybacks to avoid dilution.

The hosts see the moat in a 20-year archive of pseudonymous, human-written content curated by unpaid volunteer moderators, with contextual ads that match users' intent-driven conversations and convert better.

Management's push toward a logged-in-only experience is read as both defensive and offensive, since logged-in (especially US) users retain better and are worth far more than casual search visitors; AI machine translation and the on-platform Answers tool are cited as growth levers.
They flag risks including reliance on volunteer moderators and concentrated insider voting power that leaves public shareholders dependent on the CEO's execution and capital allocation.
podcast: The Investor's Podcast (We Study Billionaires)  - The Investor’s Podcast Network
title: TIP861: Reddit (RDDT): Record Cash Flow, Collapsing Share Price w/ Kyle Grieve & Shawn O'Malley
